summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 25%), ICD, chronic kidney disease, and diabetes was admitted for acute shortness of breath and orthopnea worsened by recent salt intake. Evaluation revealed interstitial pulmonary edema on chest X-ray, elevated BNP, and no acute ischemia. He was treated with IV furosemide and torsemide, achieving over 3 liters of diuresis and symptomatic improvement. His oxygen saturation stabilized above 93% on room air. Diabetes was managed with insulin during admission, and oral glipizide was resumed at discharge. Warfarin was continued, though INR remained subtherapeutic at 1.4, prompting an additional dose and emphasis on follow-up monitoring. He was discharged home with instructions to maintain a low-salt diet, monitor daily weights, and follow up with cardiology and primary care.
